Hi Julia / Tom,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Per our discussion, attaching the Order Form v2 and a marked MSA with the publicity and confidentiality sections highlighted (see attached). Two quick things we want to confirm so Legal can proceed with a final redline:

Hi Marcus — thanks for the summary and the attachments. I've shared the MSA redline with our legal team and attached their marked copy (Copperlane_MSA_markup.pdf) — key items below: 

1) Embargo / announcement timing: We can't commit to a 30-day automatic approval window for all announcements. Our legal prefers a 60-day default for enterprise accounts with optional faster timelines for product-led campaigns. Can Redwood accept a 60-day standard embargo, with the option to accelerate to 30 days by mutual written consent?

2) Logo usage: We can allow the Copperlane logo on your Customers page and in a marketing case study, subject to the following: (a) Copperlane marketing must approve final creative, (b) no use in paid ads, and (c) the Copperlane logo must be displayed per our style guide. Approval should be routed to marketing@copperlane.com (or to me directly if needed).

3) Testimonial / quote: We need a two-step approval: (i) factual accuracy review (2 business days) and (ii) legal sign-off if the quote references financial terms or specific metrics.

4) Confidentiality carveouts: We cannot agree to broad publicity carveouts that waive confidentiality for deliverables or pricing. Any exception must be narrowly tailored and mutually agreed in writing.

We used track changes for the items above. If Lauren can propose specific language for the embargo clause and the two-step quote approval flow, that would help speed things up. Also, can you confirm whether Redwood requires any badge or partner-level naming in the Order Form for referral/partner listings?

Thanks,
Julia Ramos
Dir., Strategic Partnerships
Copperlane Technologies

Marcus / Julia — looping in from Legal. Thanks for the clear points, Julia. Below are two alternative snippets we can include in the MSA (pick one) so Copperlane can choose the level of control they're comfortable with. I also attached a draft PDF (Redwood_proposed_publicity_snippets.pdf).

Option A (preferred by Redwood/legal):
"Customer grants Redwood the limited right to display Customer's name and logo on Redwood's website and in marketing collateral, subject to Customer's brand guidelines and prior written approval of final materials. Customer approval shall not be unreasonably withheld and shall be provided within 10 business days of submission. Customer may request a 30- day embargo from the Effective Date for public announcements.

Option B (customer-preferred tighter control):
"Customer grants Redwood the right to display Customer's name and logo on Redwood's website and in marketing collateral, subject to Customer's brand guidelines and prior written approval of final materials. Approval shall be provided by Customer's marketing contact (email: marketing@copperlane.com) within 2 business days. Any public announcement shall be subject to a 60-day embargo from the Effective Date unless otherwise agreed in writing.

On testimonial/quote approval: we propose two discrete approvals — (1) factual accuracy within 2 business days and (2) legal approval if the quote includes commercial metrics or pricing. We recommend tightening "no use in paid ads" to exclude co-branded paid campaigns unless separately agreed.

Internal note to Marcus: If Copperlane selects Option B with a 60-day embargo and strict no-paid-ads provision, this increases go-to-market friction. We should document the impact for the deal desk (potential delay to launch, reduced marketing lift). Karthik — can you assess any resale/partner badge requirements in the Order Form?

Lauren Bishop
